Primary_Lighting_Directive.Read_First: This directive is read BEFORE every preservation rule below and wins over all of them on the single question of lighting.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Core: This is a RE-RENDER from a single light, NOT a light added on top of the photo. Mental model: treat the photo as a 3D scene; switch OFF all illumination so the scene is momentarily unlit; place exactly ONE new key light directly BELOW the subject at the vertical nadir (-90 degrees), beam aimed straight upward, with the horizontal direction disabled; then render the whole image using ONLY that one light plus ordinary ambient fill. The original photo's lighting is not dimmed, not blended and not subtracted -- it simply never participates in this new render, because the only light sources in the scene now are the new key and ambient fill. Consequence on the SUBJECT'S OWN BODY: downward-facing surfaces and undersides are directly lit and become the brightest (the underside of the chin, jaw, nose and lip if a face is present; the bottom planes, overhangs and recesses of any object), while upward-facing planes (forehead, cheekbones, tops of the head, shoulders, tops of objects) turn away from the key and are rendered by ambient fill alone, falling into upward shadow. Whatever bright/dark pattern the subject had before is gone automatically, not because you erased it, but because the light that drew it is no longer in the scene. If the subject still carries the original look, you re-rendered on top of the old light instead of replacing it, and the edit has FAILED.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Meaning_Of_Preserve: Every 'preserve / keep / do not change / unchanged' rule below protects SHAPE, GEOMETRY, ANATOMY, COLOR and TEXTURE ONLY. None of them protect the original brightness, the original flat/front lighting, or the original shadow pattern. Re-lighting the subject is REQUIRED, not optional.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Single_Light_Source_Rule: After this edit the scene contains exactly ONE key light (the new selected light, directly below the subject at the vertical nadir) plus ambient fill -- nothing else. The original key light has been removed from the scene entirely, so it casts nothing: every highlight and every shadow in the output must be explainable by the new bottom key or by ambient fill alone. This is the whole instruction; there is no list of specific shadows to delete, because you are not deleting anything -- you are rendering a scene lit only from directly below, and any plane the new key does not reach (upward-facing surfaces and top planes) is simply ambient-filled. Test for correctness: pick any shadow or highlight in the result and ask 'which light made this?' If the only honest answer is 'the original light that is supposed to be gone' (e.g. an original top-driven highlight on the forehead or hair, an original front-driven shadow beside the nose), then you have wrongly kept the old light layered under the new one -- that is the failure to avoid. Geometry, anatomy, color and texture are unaffected by this rule and stay exactly as in the original; only which light is illuminating them changes.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Carriers: The new light shows on whichever carriers are present: (1) the SUBJECT'S OWN VOLUME -- ALWAYS present, the primary proof of direction, mandatory even for floating or background-less subjects; (2) any real SHADOW-RECEIVING SURFACE -- cast shadow follows the selected direction; (3) the BACKGROUND -- restoring its true luminance so the subject separates is the new light acting on it, not a separate effect. Express the direction on every carrier that exists; never leave the subject's own volume unchanged.

Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, RE-RENDER the image's illumination from a single new key light plus ambient fill, replacing (not adding to) the original lighting, while never changing the content. Apply Primary_Lighting_Directive first, then Original_Image_Preservation_Block, Subject_Preservation_Rule, Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule, Lighting_Effect_Block, Advanced_Light_Direction_Control, Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule, Light_Intensity_Control, Environment_Lighting_Control, Light_Color_Control, Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule, and Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule. When Switch is off, ignore this entire block.

Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Rule: Keep original image structure, aspect ratio, canvas size, framing, camera angle, perspective, crop boundary, subject scale and position, background layout, object placement, geometry, silhouettes, contours, spatial/depth/overlap relationships, color identity, material/skin/hair/fabric/background texture, surface detail, grain, noise and overall composition. The subject, background, props, clothing, accessories, body parts, hair, facial features and contours must not be moved, resized, duplicated, removed, replaced, redrawn, warped, rotated, cropped, reframed, zoomed, reshaped, recolored or recomposed. Only lighting attributes -- shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction/intensity, modeling, shadow softness/density, cast-shadow behavior and environmental brightness -- may be adjusted. Lighting may change perceived brightness and contrast but must not regenerate content.
Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Negative_Rule: No stretching, squeezing, warping, liquify, reshaping, slimming, enlarging, rotating, tilting, added canvas area, face/body reconstruction, pose/hand correction, perspective correction, auto-crop, zoom, reframing, object/background replacement, added/removed objects, style reinterpretation, or retouching beyond lighting-related highlight and shadow changes.

Subject_Preservation_Rule.Applicability: Applies to any identity-bearing living subject (person, character, animal, creature). For products, objects, architecture, interiors, landscapes, vehicles, food or still life, do not force face/eye/anatomy/skin/clothing rules; instead preserve their shape, proportions, material, text, logos, labels, structure, layout, surface detail, seams and edges. For scenes preserve terrain, sky, water, plants, roads, atmosphere, background structure and natural depth. Do not force person-specific lighting onto non-person scenes.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Preserve: Keep the exact original identity and recognizability (same person/animal/character; same age, gender presentation, ethnicity cues, personality, character design); same face shape, proportions and anatomy -- brows, eyes, nose, mouth, lips, teeth, jawline, chin, cheekbones, wrinkles, pores, freckles, scars, moles, makeup, facial hair, skin texture and expression; same body shape, proportions, head-to-body ratio, neck, shoulders, torso, limbs, hands, fingers, feet, posture, gesture, pose and silhouette; same hairstyle, length, volume, hairline, direction, texture and color; same clothing design, fit, folds, color, fabric, logos, patterns, accessories, jewelry, glasses, hats, bags, props and object interactions; same subject scale, position, crop boundary, framing, orientation, contact points and subject-to-background relationship. This rule fixes geometry, color and texture only -- it does NOT fix brightness, lighting or shadow.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Eye_Gaze: If eyes are present, strictly preserve the original eye gaze, direction, line of sight, pupil and iris position, eyelid shape and openness, eye expression, catchlight position and emotional intent; do not make the subject look at the camera if they were not, or look away if they were, and do not change eye focus, contact, squinting or blinking. Lighting may change highlights and shadows around the eyes only. If no eyes are present, ignore this and preserve the actual visible content.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Allowed_Changes: Only lighting attributes change: shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction and intensity, modeling brightness and hardness, shadow density and softness, cast-shadow behavior. Per Primary_Lighting_Directive the face, skin and body MUST be visibly re-lit; identity, anatomy, texture and color stay the same.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Negative_Rule: No identity/face/expression/gaze/pose change; no body shape or proportion change; no hairstyle or hair-color change; no clothing or accessory change; no hand/finger/anatomy correction; no beautification, skin smoothing, airbrushing, slimming, aging, de-aging, stylization, realism reinterpretation, character redesign or person replacement; no retouching beyond lighting highlight and shadow changes.

Lighting_Control.Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule: Apply the selected light direction to all visible subjects, objects and environment surfaces by their actual geometry. Surfaces facing the new key receive it directly; surfaces turned away from it are rendered by ambient fill; vertical planes, object sides, furniture, architecture, vehicles, foliage, terrain, folds, cavities, recesses, edges and corners follow the same selected direction, falloff and material response. Preserve all original shapes, materials, textures, colors, proportions and spatial relationships. Material response is governed by optical type regardless of direction: opaque solids (stone, metal, wood, plastic, dense fabric) block light into hard-edged highlights and shadow boundaries, with sharp speculars on metal/glossy/wet and diffuse falloff on matte; translucent or thin materials (glass, sheer gauze, thin fabric, leaves, petals, ears, skin and hair edges) transmit and scatter it, glowing with soft subsurface bleed and luminous edge transmission. Apply the matching behavior to whatever material is present, preserving original color and texture.
Lighting_Control.Lighting_Effect_Block: Re-render the image as a scene lit by a SINGLE new key light positioned directly BELOW the subject/object/scene at the vertical nadir (-90 degrees), beam aimed straight upward, plus ambient fill -- the original illumination is removed from the scene and contributes nothing, so it is replaced, not layered under the new light. Every highlight and shadow in the result must be explainable by the new bottom key or by ambient fill alone; none may trace back to the original lighting. Preserve subject identity (if people/animals present), facial features, expression, eye gaze, skin/fur texture, body structure, pose, clothing, accessories, props, product shape, text, logos, architecture, furniture, landscape elements, background, composition, original color palette and material/photographic texture. Build clear underlight modeling: downward-facing surfaces and undersides brightest, upward-facing planes falling into upward shadow, with cast shadows projecting upward from lower protrusions, cavities and overhangs; no leftover patch may trace back to the old light. Photorealistic, pure lighting adjustment only: no fog, haze, extra objects, geometry/subject/face/eye-gaze/pose/clothing change, product or architecture redesign, scene-layout change, recoloring, color cast, background light spots, projected patches, spotlight circles, lens flare, glow blobs, or artificial halos.

Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Rule: Treat the main subject/object/scene center as the center of an imaginary sphere. The light source sits on that sphere and points toward the visible content. Use ONLY pure vertical bottom_minus_90 lighting: the horizontal direction is DISABLED and must not influence the result -- do not reinterpret it as front, back, left, right or any diagonal, and do not turn it into a lower-front / front-bottom / diagonal horror or portrait beauty light. The key must sit directly below the subject at the vertical nadir with the beam aimed straight upward. Express the position through highlight placement on downward-facing surfaces and undersides, upward shadow on upper-facing planes, upward cast-shadow direction, surface-facing illumination and environmental consistency. Do not alter the original geometry, composition, text, logos or material identity while changing direction.
Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Ignore_Unselected_Rule: Horizontal_Position_Options and Vertical_Position_Options are a reference menu only. Apply ONLY the option named in Selected_Horizontal_Position / Selected_Vertical_Position. All other options are inactive references and must NOT influence the lighting direction, highlights, shadows or cast shadow behavior.

Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Override_Note: OVERRIDES the lighting implied by every preservation rule above: those rules protect SHAPE, GEOMETRY, COLOR and TEXTURE only, never the original brightness, flat/even lighting or shadow pattern. The subject MUST be re-lit and MUST visibly gain new shadows from the selected direction, while identity, anatomy and texture stay unchanged.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Rule: The image is re-rendered as a scene lit by ONE new key light plus ambient fill; the old light is gone from the scene, so the new lighting replaces it rather than being added on top. The change MUST be clearly visible on each carrier present: (1) the SUBJECT'S OWN VOLUME -- downward-facing planes and undersides directly lit by the bottom key while upward-facing planes are rendered by ambient fill alone; ALWAYS present and mandatory for floating, isolated or background-less subjects, where it is the ONLY way to read the direction. Because the original key is no longer in the scene, no original bright/dark patch may survive -- in particular no original top-driven forehead/hair highlight or front-driven nose-side shadow on a now differently-lit plane; its old pattern is simply absent, not erased. (2) any real SHADOW-RECEIVING SURFACE -- cast and form shadows project UPWARD from lower protrusions, undersides, cavities and overhangs. (3) the BACKGROUND -- when too bright for separation, its true luminance is restored. Do not artificially darken or brighten either side -- render the real physical result. The result must look clearly relit and different from the original in light and shadow, while remaining the exact same subject, geometry, color, texture and composition.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Surface_Absence_Rule: If a shadow-receiving surface is genuinely absent or too far to catch a realistic cast shadow (subject against open sky, a seamless backdrop or a gradient), do not fabricate fake ground or background shadows; in that case the subject's own volume alone must carry the full directional effect. When a valid surface IS present, the cast shadow and the subject modeling must show the change together.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Negative_Rule: Do not output flat, even, frontal, ambient or original-style uniform lighting on the subject; do not let the new key still illuminate planes as if from the original direction; do not let the subject look unchanged from the original; do not treat 'preserve identity/skin/face' as a reason to skip re-lighting; do not issue brightness-operation instructions such as 'darken / dim / brighten / lift / crush / reduce fill on one side' -- describe only the physics (one new key from the selected position, planes turned away rendered by ambient fill) and let the shading be the natural result; do not render rim as a flat graphic stroke, sticker outline, neon border or detached halo; do not add fake background shadows on sky or seamless backdrops; do not express the direction on only one carrier while leaving the subject's own volume unchanged.

Horizontal_Position_Options.front: light source directly in front of the subject on the horizontal plane, aligned with the camera. Rays travel front to back. Front surfaces receive soft even illumination, rear surfaces fall only slightly into shadow, cast shadows extend minimally behind. Clean frontal lighting with minimal left-right bias.
Horizontal_Position_Options.front_right: light source at the front-right, about 45 degrees from front. Rays travel diagonally from front-right. Front-right surfaces receive the strongest illumination, left and rear surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the back-left. Three-quarter frontal lighting with right-side modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.right: light source directly to the right, about 90 degrees from front. Rays travel horizontally right to left. Right-facing surfaces receive the strongest illumination, left-facing fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the left. Strong right-side lighting with clear lateral modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back_right: light source at the back-right, about 135 degrees from front. Rays travel diagonally from back-right. Back-right surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-left surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the front-left. Rear three-quarter lighting with edge separation and partial silhouette.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back: light source directly behind the subject on the horizontal plane at 0-degree vertical elevation, opposite the camera. Rays travel horizontally back to front toward the camera. Back-facing surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-facing surfaces no longer receive the key light and read as the side turned away from it, cast shadows extend toward the camera/front. Pure horizontal backlighting with strong silhouette structure.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back_left: light source at the back-left, about 135 degrees from front on the left. Rays travel diagonally from back-left. Back-left surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-right surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the front-right. Rear three-quarter lighting with edge separation and partial silhouette.
Horizontal_Position_Options.left: light source directly to the left on the horizontal plane at 0-degree elevation, about 90 degrees from front. Rays travel horizontally left to right. Left-facing surfaces receive the strongest illumination, right-facing fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the right. Pure horizontal side lighting with clear lateral modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.front_left: light source at the front-left, about 45 degrees from front. Rays travel diagonally from front-left. Front-left surfaces receive the strongest illumination, right and rear surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the back-right. Three-quarter frontal lighting with left-side modeling.

Vertical_Position_Options.top_90: light source directly above the subject at +90 degrees elevation, pure zenith, beam aimed vertically downward. Strongest highlights on upward-facing surfaces, top planes and upper edges; side surfaces darker; undersides, recesses and lower planes fall into deep shadow. Cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath. Ignore horizontal direction.
Vertical_Position_Options.upper_45: light source above the subject at about +45 degrees elevation, between horizontal and top, beam aimed diagonally downward. Upper planes and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive highlights; lower planes, undersides and opposite-facing surfaces fall into controlled shadow. Cast shadows travel diagonally downward and away.
Vertical_Position_Options.horizontal_0: light source positioned at 0 degrees elevation on the horizontal plane around the subject, at approximately mid-height. The rays travel horizontally, parallel to the ground, striking the subject from the selected horizontal position at the same vertical height, not from above or below. Surfaces facing the light are illuminated, opposite-facing surfaces fall into shadow, while top- and bottom-facing planes receive little direct light. Cast shadows extend mainly horizontally away from the selected direction. Avoid overhead and bottom-up lighting.
Vertical_Position_Options.lower_45: light source positioned below the subject at about -45 degrees elevation, halfway between the horizontal plane and the bottom pole. The rays travel diagonally upward toward the subject, not vertically. Lower-facing surfaces, undersides, bottom edges and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive stronger illumination; upper and top-facing surfaces become relatively darker but stay partially readable. Cast shadows move diagonally upward and away, following the selected horizontal position and the low angle. A low-position diagonal key light, not a pure bottom light.
Vertical_Position_Options.bottom_minus_90: light source positioned directly below the subject at -90 degrees elevation, pure nadir bottom position, beam aimed vertically upward. An extreme direct bottom light, not a diagonal low-angle light. Strongest highlights appear almost exclusively on undersides, bottom planes, lower edges and downward-facing surfaces; front, side and top-facing surfaces receive little direct light and top planes fall into deep upward shadow. Shadows project vertically upward from protrusions, cavities and overhangs. The result feels unnatural, severe and unmistakably bottom-lit. Ignore horizontal direction.

Light_Intensity_Control.Rule: Use only the selected intensity level. The Intensity_Value controls strength, contrast, shadow density, highlight brightness, shadow edge sharpness and falloff of the selected directional key light. Do not change the subject, eye gaze, direction or expression while adjusting intensity.

Intensity_Levels.20: soft low-intensity key light, gentle illumination, low contrast, light shadows, soft shadow edges, subtle highlights, weak sculptural form, natural low-power lighting
Intensity_Levels.40: moderate-low intensity key light, controlled illumination, mild contrast, visible but not harsh shadows, moderate shadow softness, restrained highlights, gentle facial sculpting
Intensity_Levels.60: medium-intensity cinematic key light, balanced contrast, clear highlight and shadow structure, defined facial volume, moderate shadow density, realistic falloff, controlled dramatic lighting
Intensity_Levels.80: strong high-intensity key light, high contrast, sharp shadow structure, dense shadows, bright highlights, strong sculptural form, dramatic directional lighting, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.90: very strong high-intensity key light, very bright highlights, high contrast, hard highlights, dense opposite-side shadows, strong separation, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.100: extreme high-intensity hard key light, very high contrast, very sharp shadow edges, deep black shadows, intense specular highlights, harsh falloff, powerful sculptural lighting, severe dramatic illumination

Environment_Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply the selected lighting direction and intensity to the subject, objects and surrounding environment/background by physical surface orientation and scene geometry. The environment may receive general brightness, exposure, contrast change, natural cast-shadow direction, directional consistency on surfaces and subtle brightness consistency, but must not generate visible light spots, projected circles, decorative patches, glow blobs, halos, lens flares or artificial bright stains. When Switch is off, apply the lighting mainly to the main visible content while preserving the original background. Do not change background objects, subject identity, object/product shape, text, logos, architecture, position, composition, eye gaze or scene layout. Environmental lighting must support the selected direction, not flatten it.
Environment_Lighting_Control.Environment_Prompt: extend the new key light into the surrounding environment only through realistic overall illumination, directional consistency on surfaces, natural cast-shadow direction projecting upward from lower protrusions and undersides, general exposure shift and subtle brightness consistency. Make visible content and environment share the same selected bottom direction and intensity. Preserve original color palette, material colors, photographic texture, atmosphere, background objects, subject identity, face and gaze if present, body/clothing/pose, product shape, text, logos, geometry, architecture, landscape structure and composition. No light spots, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flare, glow blobs, artificial halos, decorative patterns or lamp effects on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture or background; no colored spill or tint; no object/subject/product/architecture/scene-layout change; no gaze change if eyes present.

Lighting_Control.Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule: If the background is pure white, near-white, overexposed or too bright for the subject/foreground to separate, the new light acting on the background carrier means reducing only the background luminance/value enough to create clear separation between the visible subject/foreground/scene contour and the background. This is part of re-lighting (the light reaching the background carrier), not a separate effect. Preserve original hue, color identity, saturation relationship, material/photographic texture, background objects, structure and composition. Do not recolor the background, add color cast or colored light, change geometry, add objects, or change the subject/scene. The adjustment must behave like exposure/value reduction only, not color grading, and must support readability without overriding the selected direction.
Lighting_Control.Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule: Do not create any visible light spots, patches, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flares, glow blobs, artificial halos, bright stains, colored light marks, caustic patterns, bokeh spots, decorative illumination or lamp effects on the background. The background may only receive realistic overall brightness, exposure, contrast and natural shadow changes from the selected key direction. Preserve original background texture, color identity, surface material, object structure and composition. Do not add new light shapes or patterns on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture, objects or any background surface.

Light_Color_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply Main_Light_Color to the selected directional key light. When off, ignore this entire Light_Color_Control block and keep the light color natural or unchanged.
Light_Color_Control.Effect_Block: ignored because Light_Color_Control is off; no color gel lighting, no artificial colored light, no warm yellow overlay, no red tint, no blue tint, preserve natural or original light color
